title: Voynich manuscript
caveat: These are questions about the material that can be measured before anyone proposes a reading. Answering all of them would not decipher the script; it would make a later claim testable. Nothing here is a reading, and no probability of decipherment is assigned.

lay.tagline: A 15th-century illustrated book in a script nobody can read.
lay.summary: The Voynich manuscript is a book of about 240 pages held at Yale, written in an unknown script and full of drawings of plants, stars and bathing figures. Its vellum has been carbon dated to the early 1400s. Nobody knows whether it hides a real language, a cipher or no meaning at all. We have not proposed a reading. The plan is to measure first how much the statistics change when you change how the script is transcribed.
lay.what_it_is: The script uses perhaps 20 to 30 distinct signs, written in what look like words. Researchers turn it into Roman letters using schemes such as EVA, but those letters are labels for shapes, not sounds, and different schemes split the signs differently.
lay.what_we_found: Three of four structural questions are measured and the first cipher-shaped test now has both of its declared measurements. The declared statistics survive both transcription choice and word segmentation (glyph frequency agreement 0.999; sign frequencies exactly invariant under every segmentation). The held-out test answered yes: unseen folios are predicted better than every one of 1,000 declared shuffles, with the transferable structure concentrating inside words. The substitution screen's first pass was indeterminate by its own declared rule; its calibrated pass then measured the cross-text penalty at only 0.018 to 0.060 nats per pair, and the real text stood below the calibrated band in all six (file, language) cells, by roughly 2 to 10 times that penalty, in all three transcriptions. The band was then widened to three English and four Latin class members (including the period-appropriate 1485 Malory and three centuries of Latin prose), every one of 35 seeded plants stayed above the real text in all six cells, and the period-appropriate member scored strongest rather than weakest, so archaic style does not explain the gap. A trigram-resolution re-scoring of the same band then found the same shape again: thirty planted substitutions recovered their anchors exactly, the destroyed-adjacency floors stayed below the real text, and the real text sat below every best-recovered band member in all six cells by 3.6 to 8.8 times the measured cross-text penalty - trigrams carry about three times the bigram resolution, and the verdicts split three to three only because six stuck computer-draws on one reference text (a disclosed machinery artifact, recorded as such) gave the rule a lower anchor at noise level. The class as scoped is still not excluded - the population is sampled, not the class - but no sampled member of it explains the text at either resolution, and the next declared measurement is a band with the machinery noise removed by design. No conclusion about language or meaning is drawn.
lay.whats_next: Family 4's declared fifth measurement: a noise-controlled trigram band - the restart budget raised as a declared parameter and a per-text convergence criterion declared before the run, so band membership rests on machine draws that agree; if the real text stays below that band's recovered members in all six cells, the exclusion of the scoped class becomes declinable in its own declared format, with the bigram and trigram artifacts behind it.

faq.q: Has the Voynich manuscript been deciphered?
faq.a: No. Many readings have been announced; none has been shown to work on pages its author did not use to build it.
It is not settled. The vellum is old, but that does not tell us whether the text means anything.

researcher.summary: Beinecke MS 408. Transliteration ZL 3b (IVTFF 2.0, 13 May 2025) from voynich.nu, to be compared with a second independently authored transliteration. Planned statistics: sign n-grams of orders 1 to 4, token lengths and line-position effects under each declared segmentation, with at most 2,000 seeded nulls preserving word lengths or line lengths, and 10 reserved folios.
methods: Declared substitution screen with plant and floor bands

statuses.closed-with-power: Answered with a control: measured on a frozen corpus, with a solved or synthetic control showing the method works.
statuses.tested-without-power: Measured without a control: a number exists, but no control shows what it would look like if the answer were different.
statuses.open: Open: proposed here, not yet measured.

families.family: Do the statistics survive a change of transcription?
families.evidence: Measured 20 October 2026 on the 5,013 worded loci shared by ZL 3b and IT 2a outside ten reserved whole folios. Spearman rank correlation over shared types: glyph frequency 0.999, bigrams 0.965, trigrams 0.937, quadgrams 0.915, word tokens 0.901. Glyph totals match within 218 of 184,310; the files split 34,354 and 36,441 tokens (6.1 percent), so the residue is segmentation, not the statistics. Controls: the within-file half-split resampling baseline is 0.73 for word tokens and 0.84 to 1.00 for the rest, so the cross-transcription agreement is at or above the metric's own ceiling; a planted cyclic relabelling of the ten most frequent EVA characters of IT drops bigram agreement to 0.40, trigrams to 0.10, quadgrams to -0.07 and words to 0.26, margins of 0.56 or more; planted miniature files control the pipeline itself. Nothing follows about language or meaning.

families.family: Do they survive a change of word segmentation?
families.evidence: Measured 20 October 2026 on the same 5,013 worded shared loci under two declared segmentations: the frozen long-word convention (delegated to the frozen parser and locked to it on every locus of all three files) and the identical normalisation with every uncertain space cut as definite. IT carries no uncertain spaces, so its two policies agree exactly: a built-in zero-join control. ZL has 2,603 joins: tokens 34,354 to 36,957, the delta exactly the join count; word types fall 8,988 to 7,959 (splitting recycles joined hapaxes, so a large share of measured vocabulary size is segmentation); mean length 5.365 to 4.987. GC behaves the same with 2,321 joins. Sign frequencies are exactly invariant (delta 0 in every file). Word-frequency ranks move to rho 0.942 (ZL) and 0.947 (GC) between their own two policies, not collapse. Cross-file ZL-IT agreement holds at 0.90 or better at every order under both policies, and the split values are all at or above the long-word values (word tokens 0.901 to 0.915), so family 1's conclusion does not depend on segmentation. Planted synthetic loci reproduce the exact token-delta identity. No reading and no language claim.

families.family: Does the text predict unseen folios better than shuffled text?
families.evidence: Measured 20 October 2026 under pre-declared statistics, nulls, seeds and verdict rules. Ten whole folios reserved statistics-blind (f87r, f96v, f95r2, f68v1, f32v, f106r, f67r1, f36r, f82v, f24r) were scored against 1,000 seeded permutations per cell in three files of independent authorship: every cell's real statistic sat below all 1,000 null values, p 0.0010, the budget's floor. Within-word glyph-order structure transferred at 30 to 39 percent below the null floor; word-adjacency structure transferred weakly but beyond all noise at 0.5 to 0.8 percent below the null floor, so most transferable structure lives inside words. Machinery power demonstrated in both directions on planted synthetic corpora; stored null heads and real statistics recompute exactly from the declared per-replicate seeds. This is a necessary condition for language-like structure, not a sufficient one; no language, cipher or meaning conclusion follows. The reservation's testing role is discharged; family 4 must declare its own held-out discipline.

families.family: Is it a simple cipher of a known language?
families.evidence: First measurement 20 October 2026: the declared substitution screen (one-to-one substitution with carried word divisions, the alphabet's cipher symbols inside the file's most frequent glyph characters up to 26 plus the word-boundary mark, add-one bigram scoring, greedy swap search with 16 seeded restarts, plants and floors per cell) against two frozen reference proeses, English (Pride and Prejudice, Gutenberg 1342) and Latin (Augustinus Confessiones, Gutenberg 33849). All six (file, language) cells scored indeterminate per the declared rule: real best sits 0.11 to 0.31 nats per counted pair below plant self-parity and 1.17 to 1.33 nats per counted pair above its own destroyed-adjacency floors, consistent across ZL, GC and IT. Plants reached parity exactly 20 of 20 times, so the machinery recognizes a substitution when the material is one. Second measurement the same day, the declared cross-text calibration against second reference proeses (English: Frankenstein, Gutenberg 84; Latin: C. Iuli Caesaris De Bello Gallico I-IV, Gutenberg 218): the measured cross-text penalty is only 0.018 to 0.060 nats per pair, and the real text stands below the cross band in all six cells, by 0.094 to 0.189 nats per pair (English) and 0.159 to 0.254 (Latin) - roughly 2 to 10 times the measured cross penalty - with the Latin cross plants cut shorter than the real streams and still scoring above them. Verdict per the declared rule: below-cross-band, all six cells. Not yet family closure: the band is two proeses per language and period styles are outside the sampled population (abbreviated scribal usage remains outside the declared class). Not covered by either unit: homophonic or polyalphabetic substitution, word-level ciphers, transpositions, nulls, abbreviations. No mapping is published; nothing here is a reading. Third measurement 21 October 2026, the declared widened band declared after the cross screen and before this run: five added class members frozen with sha256 provenance and identical declared processing - English: Moby Dick (Gutenberg 2701) and Le Morte D'Arthur volume 1 (the 1485 Caxton prose, the band's period-appropriate member, Gutenberg 1251); Latin: Vulgate Daniel (828), Colloquium heptaplomeres (17859), and De Rariorum Animalium atque Stirpium Historia (27655). The cross screen's own texts replay their declared per-plant seeds and recompute their cross-artifact values exactly; the added texts use declared sequential rngs per (file, language, text). All 35 plants converged to one value each, the band's weakest edge moved from -5.1345 (Caesar) to -5.2063 (Rariorum) in Latin and from -5.1603 (Frankenstein) to -5.1893 (Moby Dick) in English, and the real text still stands below every band member in all six cells, now by 0.064 to 0.165 nats per pair (English) and 0.087 to 0.182 (Latin), still 1.17 to 1.33 above the recomputed floors. The period-appropriate Malory scored the strongest plant values (about -5.10), not the weakest, so archaic style does not explain the gap at bigram resolution; the band's weakest members are the two short Latin texts (under 78 thousand symbols against the real streams' 218k to 220k), yet their plants still score above the real text under that length handicap. Verdict per the rule declared before the run: below-widened-band, all six cells. Not yet family closure: the sampled population is three English and four Latin proeses, not the class. Not covered by any unit: homophonic or polyalphabetic substitution, word-level ciphers, transpositions, nulls, abbreviations. No mapping is published; nothing here is a reading. Fourth measurement the same day, the declared trigram resolution pass declared in its docstring before the run: identical streams, mapped set and search machinery, re-scored under the declared add-one trigram model of the first references (P(third | first, second) = (n + 1) / (n(second pair) + 27)). Self-parity plants reached their truncated-stream anchors exactly (30 of 30), every floor stayed below the real by 0.36 to 0.72 nats per trigram, and the real text stands below every best-recovered band member in all six cells by 0.5321 to 1.0763 nats per trigram, which is 3.6 to 8.8 times the measured trigram cross-text penalty (0.121 to 0.147 nats per trigram). The declared rule's verdict strings split - three English cells consistent-with-substitution, three Latin cells below-trigram-band - through a disclosed machinery reason: six of forty-five English cross-plant draws (five Moby Dick, one Frankenstein in GC) stuck near the floors' region on identical data whose healthy draws recover about 0.9 nats higher, so the English rule outcome rode on stuck draws rather than member statistics, while all Latin draws converged within 0.0001. The class is not excluded by this artifact's rule alone; the declared next instrument is the noise-controlled trigram band.
families.next: The declared fifth measurement: a noise-controlled trigram band - same streams, model and search, with the restart budget raised as a declared parameter and a declared per-text convergence criterion (a band member enters the band only when its plant draws agree to within 0.0001 nats; failing texts are recorded as such and do not set the threshold). If the real text stays below that band’s recovered members in all six cells, the exclusion of the scoped class becomes declinable in its own declared format, with the bigram and trigram artifacts behind it.
